blocks.text: Drug A Versus Placebo: a Report with Inconsistent Numbers

This was a multicentre, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. Adults aged 18 years or older with hypertension were eligible. Exclusion criteria included pregnancy and severe renal disease. A total of 238 patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive Drug A 10 mg once daily (n = 120) or placebo (n = 118). Patients were followed for 12 months. The primary outcome was major cardiovascular events at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included all-cause death and change in systolic blood pressure. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.

The primary outcome occurred in 24 of 120 patients (20.0%) in the Drug A group and 36 of 118 patients (30.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.41 to 0.94; P = 0.02). Serious adverse events occurred in 130 of 120 patients in the Drug A group. The odds ratio for withdrawal was 1.8 (95% CI 2.1 to 3.0; P = 1.30).
